newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates steady to higher.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates were steady to slightly higher in poor trade on Tuesday, dealers said.
Demand for kuna funds was low at 24 million kuna although two million were left unsettled due to lack of money on offer.
"Banks' accounts emptied over the weekend and have so far not recovered enough so supply is still poor," one dealer said.

Call money loans accounted for more than a half of the 22 million kuna, settled by mid-morning. The rate was 10 percent, unchanged from last Friday's average 10 percent, save for a smaller loan struck at 10.5 percent.
Term rates firmed slightly, varying between 10 percent for one-week funds and 18 percent for two- and three-month borrowings.
The central bank's Lombard lending was 23.6 million kuna, down from 30.6 million on Monday.
Dealers put overnight trade on Tuesday at 61 million kuna granted to two banks for maintenance of their mandatory reserves. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
